newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CHARLTON PLAYER TESTS POSITIVE FOR DRUG COCKTAIL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHARLTON PLAYER TESTS POSITIVE FOR DRUG COCKTAIL.

text.p: An 18-year-old midfielder at English first division club Charlton Athletic was suspended from playing on Monday after testing positive for cocaine, cannabis and Ecstasy.

Jay Notley was the first player to test positive from around 300 tested this season. He was charged with misconduct by the Football Association and suspended immediately pending his appearance before a disciplinary commission.

Notley is the third Charlton youngster to test positive for drugs in the last 20 months following Dean Chandler and Lee Bowyer, now at Leeds, last year. They both tested positive for cannabis and were given counselling.

The club's executive director Jonathan Fuller said on Monday: "We have made rigorous efforts to educate all our players, from schoolboys upwards, of the dangers of drugs through lectures, discussions and the issuing of appropriate literature.
"Only last week we arranged a meeting with the parents of our young players and the local police to talk about the dangers of drugs.
"We at Charlton are determined to do all we can to help get drugs out of football. It is clearly a social problem which we must do all we can to keep out of the game."
An FA spokesman said: "It is the first time we have come across a cocktail of drugs like this so it is obviously a serious matter.
"Cocaine and Ecstasy are class A drugs, and cocaine is a performance enhancing drug too."
But he insists football appears to be winning the fight to clean up the game of the drug menace.
"Two seasons ago there were 12 positive results from 272 tests. Last season there were seven from the same number of tests.
"This season we have stepped up our testing to around 500 and this is the first positive result from around 300 already carried out, which is encouraging. But we cannot afford to be complacent.
"Our aim is to focus on the professionals and in particular the younger players who are most likely to be at risk from drugs."
